answer: New agents cannot immediately earn the same trust as established ones: each must lock a scarce deposit and complete small, independently checked tasks before receiving larger payments. A Sybil attacker can create many names, but every identity ties up capital and must produce verifiable work; splitting funds across accounts does not multiply the deposit. Failed checks forfeit the stake, while honest contributions build reputation gradually. A nectar task may send a small ripple of value across a terrace, but the attacker pays for each identity and risks losing its bond.
